name: libngspice
desc: Spice circuit simulator as shared library
why: The ngspice circuit simulator as a library; real electronics simulation, but packaged as a shared library rather than a playground.

brief.what_it_is: ngspice is an open source SPICE circuit simulator for electric and electronic circuits. Per its homepage, a circuit is written as a netlist that can include JFETs, bipolar and MOS transistors, passive R/L/C elements, diodes, transmission lines, and digital gates, including mixed-signal circuits. Input is command-line or file based, with no schematic entry. Output is one or more graphs of currents, voltages and other quantities, or a data file. The brew entry libngspice is the shared-library form of this simulator; the pages I read describe the simulator itself and do not describe the library interface.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents ngspice as an open source alternative for simulating electric and electronic circuits in the SPICE tradition, and says it aims to be SPICE compatible so existing PSPICE, LTSPICE and HSPICE (foundry PDK) models and netlists can be used. The README frames it as a successor built from Spice3f5, Cider1b1 and Xspice, with many contributors beyond those packages.
brief.how_it_works: The README says ngspice is a mixed-level/mixed-signal simulator combining Spice3f5 (analog circuit simulation), Cider1b1 (coupling to the DSIM device simulator for device-structure-level accuracy), and Xspice (code-model support and event-driven digital simulation). The homepage says digital parts are event driven. I did not find any description of how the shared library exposes this to other programs.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says Windows source and binaries are on the SourceForge download page, that popular Linux distributions, Cygwin and FreeBSD packages exist, and that Homebrew covers macOS. Beyond brew install, I saw nothing about libraries, headers, runtimes, accounts or first-run configuration; the pages I reached do not cover the shared-library build or linking.
brief.standout: Unlike most circuit simulators with a GUI, ngspice is a plain-text netlist engine that reads both PSPICE/LTSPICE and HSPICE foundry model libraries and mixes analog and event-driven digital in one circuit. Packaging it as a shared library, as libngspice does, makes that engine embeddable in other programs, which is the part the scout notes highlight.
brief.status: Apparently maintained, though I found no release date or last-commit date. The homepage lists introductory FOSDEM talks on ngspice status and updates through FOSDEM'25, and the GitHub repository ngspice/ngspice exists with a README pointing to active mailing lists. The libngspice formula's own date was not checked.
brief.caveats: No schematic entry; users need third-party front ends for schematics. The shared-library interface is not documented on any page I reached, so the entry should not describe its API. Two guessed sub-pages (development.html and features.html) returned 404, so the homepage was the only documentation source that loaded. The homepage's FOSDEM and manual links were not followed, so the detailed manual was not read.

Ngspice is a mixed-level/mixed-signal circuit simulator.
